s: A company with 200 AWS accounts in an organization in AWS Organizations needs a monthly cost report by cost center. Resources are tagged inconsistently with keys such as CostCenter, costcenter, and cost-center, and many values do not match the official cost center list. The CostCenter tag does not appear as a filter in AWS Cost Explorer. Finance also needs the report to include the previous 6 months of costs for resources that are already tagged correctly. Which combination of steps will meet these requirements? (Select TWO.)
o: Create a tag policy in AWS Organizations that defines the CostCenter key capitalization and its allowed values, enable enforcement for supported resource types, and attach the policy to the organization root.
In each member account, activate the CostCenter cost allocation tag in the Billing and Cost Management console.
Create an AWS Config required-tags rule in every account with automatic remediation that adds a default CostCenter value to untagged resources.
Use Tag Editor to retag all resources, and wait 24 hours for historical costs to be reallocated automatically.
In the management account, activate CostCenter as a user-defined cost allocation tag, and request a cost allocation tag backfill for the previous 6 months.

w.y: Tag policies standardize key capitalization and allowed values and can prevent noncompliant tagging on supported resource types. User-defined tags appear in billing tools only after they are activated as cost allocation tags in the management (payer) account, and a cost allocation tag backfill applies them to up to 12 months of past data, covering the previous 6 months.

o.A: Correct: standardizes keys and values going forward.
o.B: In an organization, only the management account can activate cost allocation tags.
o.C: Does not fix inconsistent keys or values, assigns costs to a meaningless default, and gives no history.
o.D: Tags are not applied to past costs automatically; without activation and backfill history is not reallocated.
o.E: Correct: activation must happen in the payer account, and backfill provides the historical data.

d: include the previous 6 months of costs
